If Filter is false: compute $s = \text{rsqrt}(|\text{ddx}(UV.x) \cdot \text{ddy}(UV.y) - \text{ddy}(UV.x) \cdot \text{ddx}(UV.y)|)$; set $\text{SSR} = s / \text{TextureSize}$ [S2, unofficial].

The 'Source [S2] notes' explicitly state: 'If Filter is false: compute s = rsqrt(abs(ddx(UV.x) * ddy(UV.y) - ddy(UV.x) * ddx(UV.y))); set SSR = s / TextureSize.' This matches the claim exactly, noting that `abs` is equivalent to `|...|` and `rsqrt` is the reciprocal square root function.

An anti-aliasing technique that precomputes MIP-filtered parameters at the surfel center during preprocessing to reduce per-pixel rasterization cost while eliminating aliasing artifacts [S3, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S3]. The source explicitly states that the 'Center-precomputed MIP filter' technique precomputes the Jacobian at the surfel center during preprocessing, stores the resulting MIP-filtered inverse covariance and normalization factor (four parameters), and applies them during rasterization to reduce per-pixel cost. It also confirms that this method eliminates aliasing artifacts (Moiré patterns) and is faster than the per-pixel Jacobian evaluation method (AA-2DGS).
